question: What cathode does the anode-free full cell use, how is it prepared so that the cell contains no sodium metal on assembly, and what cathode capacity was assumed for its energy density?
expect: pyrite (FeS2), presodiated before assembly (p5.L29-41); Na1.5FeS2 stoichiometry, an FeS2 capacity of 335 mAh/g (p5.L52-53)
rendered: The anode-free full cell uses a presodiated pyrite (FeS2) cathode. To prepare it, the pyrite cathode is first presodiated prior to cell assembly. This is done to introduce sodium ions into the pyrite cathode, allowing it to function as a cathode in the anode-free full cell configuration. The cathode capacity was assumed to be 335 mAh/g, corresponding to a stoichiometry of Na1.5FeS2.
